<thought>Based on the observed mass spectrum, the isotope pattern shows a prominent M+1 peak (~16 % of the base peak) consistent with many carbon atoms, a modest M+2 peak (~5–6 % of the base peak) characteristic of sulfur (34S ≈ 4 % natural abundance), and no M+2 peak of the magnitude expected for chlorine or bromine. Therefore, the elements that can be definitively identified from the isotope distribution are carbon and sulfur. The presence of carbon is evident from the sizable M+1 peak, and sulfur is indicated by the ~5 % M+2 intensity. No other element shows a distinctive isotopic signature in this spectrum.</thought>
<final_answer>['C', 'S']</final_answer>
